sections.title: 1. Ingestion gaps: AppFlow and Transfer Family

keyTerms.definition: A fully managed integration service moving data between SaaS applications and AWS services.
A fully managed file-transfer service running SFTP, FTPS, FTP, and AS2 into S3.
Syncing only changed records instead of full snapshots.
The one-time SaaS authentication that AppFlow stores in Secrets Manager.
The only endpoint type where plain FTP works.

recall.question: What is the one-line difference between AppFlow and Transfer Family?
recall.answer: AppFlow moves data between SaaS apps and AWS; Transfer Family is a managed file-transfer server for SFTP, FTPS, FTP, and AS2.

recall.question: Sync Salesforce cases into S3 for RAG: why not EventBridge?
recall.answer: EventBridge routes events; it does not do field mapping, transforms, or masking.

recall.question: Plain FTP on a public endpoint: what happens?
recall.answer: It fails; plain FTP works only on VPC-internal endpoints.

sections.title: 2. Analytics gaps: QuickSight, Neptune Analytics, Q Apps

keyTerms.definition: QuickSight's in-memory engine; imported data answers queries from memory.
The slower but always-fresh mode that reads the source per query.
A serverless graph-analytics engine for bulk computation and vector search.
A transactional graph database for live graph queries and GraphRAG.
No-code generative AI applications built inside Q Business from natural language.
The current Neptune Analytics vector API; topKByEmbedding is deprecated.

recall.question: QuickSight or OpenSearch Dashboards for S3 billing data with governed sharing?
recall.answer: QuickSight Enterprise, with SPICE, row-level security, and ML insights.

recall.question: Neptune Database or Neptune Analytics for approximate nearest-neighbor vector search?
recall.answer: Neptune Analytics; the database is the transactional engine.

recall.question: What is the current vector API name?

keyTerms.definition: Stores secrets with KMS encryption and automatic Lambda-based rotation.
The Web Application Firewall filtering HTTP requests at layer 7.
The free Bedrock runtime API that counts input tokens without running inference.
The decoding parameter limiting sampling to the k most likely tokens; not in Converse inferenceConfig.
The CloudWatch service for feature flags and A/B experiments with statistics.
Time to first token: request sent to first token received, streaming only.

recall.question: Automatically rotate a database password every 30 days with no downtime: which service?
recall.answer: Secrets Manager with automatic rotation; Parameter Store has no rotation engine.

recall.question: Why does inferenceConfig with topK 50 fail on Converse?
recall.answer: topK is not a member of Converse inferenceConfig; move it to additionalModelRequestFields.

recall.question: Which metric alarms on slow chat start with fine streaming?
recall.answer: TimeToFirstToken in AWS/Bedrock; the pause before streaming starts is TTFT.

keyTerms.definition: The managed document-analysis service for printed text, handwriting, forms, tables, and layout.
The Textract sync API for single-page documents; multi-page needs StartDocumentAnalysis.
A unique delimiter inserted between logical sections so chunking respects boundaries.
Storing vectors with fewer bits per dimension to shrink the index.
1 bit per dimension, 32 times smaller, with Hamming distance for fast search.
The SageMaker setting for how long to wait for the model artifact download.

recall.question: AnalyzeDocument on a 200-page PDF fails: what is the fix?
recall.answer: Use the async StartDocumentAnalysis with the document in S3.

recall.question: What fixes table fragments from fixed-size chunking?
recall.answer: Divider-string preprocessing at table and section boundaries, then split on the dividers.

recall.question: A 150 GB SageMaker deployment fails with a download timeout on a big-enough instance: what is the fix?
recall.answer: Increase ModelDataDownloadTimeoutInSeconds; a bigger instance does not help a timeout.
